conventions.convention: C^{k,α}(Ω) denotes the local class; C_b^{k,α}(Ω) requires the finite global norm. C^{k,α}(closure Ω) additionally requires continuous extensions of derivative fields through order k. Scaled norms weight derivative order j by R^j and the top seminorm by R^{k+α}; 0<α<1.

The nondivergence operator has positive principal part a^{ij}∂ij, real bounded coefficients, and an almost-everywhere symmetric principal matrix with λI≤A≤ΛI. Continuous coefficients extend these inequalities to frozen points. Newtonian potentials instead use −ΔΦ=δ0, giving the Hessian correction −δij f/n.

Global W^{2,p} Dirichlet estimates require 1<p<∞, a bounded C^{1,1} domain, continuous principal coefficients, and an already strong zero-trace function. The separate weak Laplacian regularity theorem assumes p>n and a bounded C^{2,α} domain. Boundary, extension and compactness uses explicitly assume AC; interior multiplier estimates assume Countable Choice.

For u_t+H(x,t,Du)=0, upper-semicontinuous subsolutions are tested at local maxima of u−φ with residual ≤0; lower-semicontinuous supersolutions are tested at local minima with residual ≥0. Initial inequalities use joint space-time limsup/liminf approaching t=0 through positive times.

A discontinuous viscosity solution is locally bounded, with its upper envelope a subsolution and its lower envelope a supersolution, both carrying the relaxed initial datum. Envelopes are pointwise functions, not almost-everywhere classes.

Whole-space comparison requires global momentum Lipschitz control and the stated C(1+|p|) space-time bound. Compact-cylinder comparison instead requires the modulus ω((1+|p|)distance) and continuous ordered parabolic boundary values. Autonomous convex superlinear comparison uses bounded uniformly continuous functions and does not require global momentum Lipschitz continuity.

L(v)=sup_p(p·v−H(p)); L may equal +∞, and p·v−(+∞) is defined as −∞ in the biconjugate. Hopf–Lax uses velocity (x−y)/t, action tL((x−y)/t), Q0=id, convex superlinear H, and bounded uniformly continuous data for solution conclusions.

G is connected, simply connected, complex semisimple, with positive Borel B=T⋉U and opposite U−. The bundle is Lλ=G×^B C_{−λ}; sections satisfy f(gb)=λ(b)f(g), and left translation is f(g0^{-1}g). Dominant sections realize L(λ)*, not L(λ). AC is assumed.

The dot action is w·λ=w(λ+ρ)−ρ; regularity tests all root coroot pairings of λ+ρ. For a simple root with n=〈λ,α∨〉≥−1, H^i(Lλ)≅H^{i+1}(L_{sα·λ}); n=−1 gives total vanishing. The canonical bundle is L_{−2ρ}, and duality replaces λ by −λ−2ρ.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. For a simple root α and λ∈X*(T), put n=〈λ,α∨〉. If n≥−1, then for every i≥0 there is a natural G-equivariant isomorphism H^i(X,Lλ)≅H^{i+1}(X,L_{sα·λ}). If n=−1 all cohomology vanishes. If n≤−1, H^{i+1}(X,Lλ)≅H^i(X,L_{sα·λ}) for every i≥0.

For continuous H on U×R^n with U open in space-time, a real upper-semicontinuous u is a subsolution when φt+H(z,Dφ)≤0 at every local maximum of u−φ, φ∈C^1(U); a real lower-semicontinuous v is a supersolution with residual ≥0 at every local minimum. Cauchy sub- and supersolutions additionally satisfy the respective joint relaxed initial inequalities.

Assume Countable Choice, n≥2 and 1<p<∞. Every u∈C_c^∞(R^n) satisfies ||D²u||p≤C(n,p)||Δu||p, with the Hessian norm the maximum of the second-derivative Lp norms; by density this extends to every u∈W^{2,p}(R^n).

Assume Countable Choice, n≥2 and 0<α<1. On BR(x0), let L be uniformly elliptic, with [A]α≤K and lower coefficients having finite global C^{0,α} bounds. If bounded u∈C²(BR) satisfies Lu=f pointwise with f∈C^{0,α}(BR), then u∈C^{2,α}(B_{R/2}) and its scaled norm is at most C(||u||∞+R²||f||∞+R^{2+α}[f]α), with C depending only on n, α, ellipticity and the stated dimensionless coefficient bounds.

Whole-space case: continuous H satisfies |H(x,t,p)−H(y,s,p)|≤C(1+|p|)(|x−y|+|t−s|) and |H(x,t,p)−H(x,t,q)|≤C|p−q|. Bounded USC subsolutions and LSC supersolutions on R^n×[0,T), with ordered initial values, satisfy u≤v in the open slab. Compact-cylinder case: under the stated ω((1+|p|)distance) bound, continuous sub- and supersolutions with ordered parabolic boundary values satisfy u≤v on the closed cylinder.

Assume AC and Countable Choice, n≥2, 0<α<1 and a bounded C^{2,α} domain Ω. For f∈C^{0,α}(closure Ω) and g∈C^{2,α}(closure Ω), the weak problem −Δu=f with u−g∈H¹0 has exactly one H¹ solution. It belongs to C^{2,α}(closure Ω), solves the equation and boundary condition classically, and satisfies ||u||_{C^{2,α}}≤C(n,α,Ω)(||f||_{C^{0,α}}+||g||_{C^{2,α}}).

For finite-valued continuous convex superlinear H and bounded uniformly continuous u0, u(x,t)=Qt u0(x) is bounded uniformly continuous on every finite closed time strip, solves ut+H(Du)=0 in viscosity sense for t>0, attains u0 locally uniformly, is the unique bounded uniformly continuous Cauchy solution, and satisfies Qt+s=QtQs.
Assume AC. For λ∈X*(T), H⁰(X,Lλ)=0 if λ is not dominant integral. If λ is dominant integral, H⁰(X,Lλ)≅L(λ)* as Lie-algebra modules and H^i(X,Lλ)=0 for every i>0.
Assume AC. For λ∈X*(T), singular λ+ρ gives H^i(X,Lλ)=0 for all i≥0. For regular λ+ρ, let w be the unique Weyl element with w·λ dominant. Then H^{ℓ(w)}(X,Lλ)≅L(w·λ)* and H^i(X,Lλ)=0 for i≠ℓ(w).

Assume Countable Choice. For Banach spaces X,Y and bounded L0,L1:X→Y, put Lt=(1−t)L0+tL1. If L0 is bijective and ||x||X≤C||Lt x||Y uniformly for t∈[0,1] and x∈X, every Lt is bijective and ||Lt^{-1}||≤C.

concerns.concern: Proof 3.1 writes the double-dual identification as “v↦(v↦f(v))”. The inner argument must be f∈V*, so the evaluation map is v↦(f↦f(v)). The following annihilator computation uses the correct map; this is a notation defect.

The first Remark says the penalty “does not change the viscosity inequality in the interior by more than the explicit strict margin η/T²”. Its derivative is η/(T−t)², which is at least η/T² and becomes unbounded near T. The Statement and Proof have the correct inequalities; the Remark reverses the bound.

seams_checked.note: Opened the weak Poisson, inhomogeneous trace-lifting and weak-solution suppliers. The global weak Schauder theorem retains AC/Countable Choice, uses the Laplace coercive specialization, and verifies the H^{1/2} trace range before invoking weak existence.

The Euler-character corollary applies the opened Weyl character formula to the dominant integral dual highest weight −w0(w·λ), retains the sign (−1)^{ℓ(w)}, and uses the completed-ring inverse only after formal cancellation. Dimension examples retain dominant-integral hypotheses.

Opened thm-hamilton-jacobi-conservation-law-correspondence-in-one-dimension. Its bounded Lipschitz potentials satisfy the BUC datum class; its convex superlinear flux uses the autonomous Hopf–Lax theorem, not momentum-Lipschitz comparison. Sup contraction is used for uniformly approximated compact-data primitives; the converse retains the −tf(0) normalization.

Opened thm-de-giorgi-nash-interior-holder-regularity. It uses the owned Hölder definition for representative and seminorm conventions; it does not infer Schauder regularity from measurable divergence-form coefficients.

Opened cor-minimisers-are-classical-when-elliptic-regularity-applies. Its Schauder branch retains n≥2, AC/Countable Choice, bounded C^{2,α} domain, Hölder forcing and C^{2,α} boundary lift. The minimizer is first identified as the weak Dirichlet solution before applying regularity.
